newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Coastal unit opens Estonian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Coastal unit opens Estonian pipeline.

text.p: Estonian Oil Service, a unit of Coastal Baltica Holding Company and Houston-based Coastal Corp, on Thursday opened a new $17 million pipeline and port facilities near the capital, Tallinn.
The pipeline and terminal will be used to move Russian oil products through Estonia to western Europe and other world markets.

"This new terminal operation will benefit the energy future of Estonia with the import and export of almost 2.5 million tonnes of petroleum products annually," David Arledge, President and Chief Executive Officer of Coastal Corp, told a news conference.
"We see Estonia as the gateway between Russia and the world markets," Arledge said.
Coastal was also planning to set up operations in Estonia's Baltic neighbours Latvia and Lithuania, as well as Poland, he added.
The refurbishment of eight fuel tanks, the construction of five new tanks and the 7.5-km pipeline will cost $17.5 million, company officials said.
Coastal in July won a tender for the privatization of Esoil, Estonia's largest fuel company, which includes a chain of service stations.
